restrictions: The online algorithm is deterministic replay of exactly the two 64-byte messages in proof.md (the all-zero block and the SAT model block); it is not a submitted generator for new collisions.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256; 1 prefix round; each message is a single 64-byte root block with flags CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT = 11, block_len 64, counter 0, standard IV, and all 256 output bits.

The cost-bearing construction is one complete CaDiCaL CDCL SAT solve of a Tseitin-encoded CNF transcribed directly from the organizer reference verifier/blake3.py (ripple-carry adders, XOR gates, rotation as wire permutation), plus model extraction and independent verification; encoding, solver work, failed branches, restarts and checking are charged once as preprocessing, with no cross-target amortization.

The construction process retired 569711958 host instructions (about 2^29.1), measured with Linux perf stat -e instructions on the complete single run; charged one-to-one as primitive word operations at 1/222 units each under collision-frontier-v5 this upper-bounds the charged preprocessing at 2^21.4 target-compression units, claimed at 2^21.
Success probability 1 is the exact probability of the deterministic replay of the mechanically verified witness; it is not model confidence and is not inferred from repeated experiment rows.
Peak simultaneously retained storage of the construction process is below 2^15.2 bytes (measured whole-process peak RSS 36884 KiB); the replay program itself retains below 2^13 bytes.
The claim extends neither to two or more BLAKE3 rounds nor to keyed BLAKE3, and claims no new differential or algebraic cryptanalysis beyond the SAT construction itself.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement by itself; the claimed scalar 22 is below the nominal display reference 128 and the incumbent 48.

heuristics.statement: The complete construction (Python CNF encoding of the one-round root compression circuit for one symbolic message, the unit-clause pinning of the second message to the all-zero block, the CaDiCaL solve, model extraction, and witness verification) executes at most 2^30 primitive word RAM operations in total, so at 1/222 units per word operation under collision-frontier-v5 the charged preprocessing is below 2^21.4, claimed at 2^21, target-compression units.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the single CaDiCaL construction run that produced the fixed two-message witness in proof.md; the deterministic replay and the organizer collision check are heuristic-free.
heuristics.extrapolation: The identical construction script was measured end-to-end with Linux perf stat -e instructions, retiring 569711958 instructions (about 2^29.1) in the complete run including Python startup, CNF generation, solve, extraction and verification; the claim rounds up to 2^30 word operations. Because one 256-bit word RAM operation requires at least one host instruction on any physical realization, the host-instruction count upper-bounds the word-operation count, and the 1/222 price then upper-bounds the charged cost.
heuristics.limitations: perf stat is not available inside the organizer container, so the instruction measurement is a disclosed, reproducible host measurement rather than an organizer-executed experiment; the exact witness relation it produced is independently rechecked by the organizer. If the true word-operation count exceeded 2^30, or the conversion argument were rejected, the claimed scalar would be invalid, though the collision witness itself remains valid.
